PF4-EXECUTE.name: Work Execution
PF4-EXECUTE.execution_order_note: ⛔ MANDATORY: Within a stage, parallel batch execution MUST be used when scope involves multiple independent items. Assess file count against batch_size BEFORE spawning any stage teammate — if file count exceeds batch_size, spawn parallel instances up to max_parallel. Do NOT default to single-instance execution when parallel batching applies. Stages themselves follow pipeline order (e.g., WS-DEV before WS-REV before WS-QA). Tasks PF4-TSK-01 and PF4-TSK-02 are sequential prerequisites before stage execution begins.
PF4-EXECUTE.subject: PF4-EXECUTE: Run work pipeline
PF4-EXECUTE.description: Execute stage pipeline for {work_type}: {pipeline}. Phase: {phase_id}, Task: {task_id}, Session: {session_id}.
PF4-EXECUTE.notes: All on-demand teammates spawned during PF4-EXECUTE remain active until PF7-END. No teammate is shut down between stages or after pipeline completion. On-demand teammates stay alive through PF5-VERIFY and PF6-COMPLETE, then are shut down at PF7-END alongside persistent teammates. This preserves context for rework loops and avoids expensive re-spawns. ⛔ MANDATORY PARALLELIZATION: Before spawning any primary stage teammate, the team lead MUST assess whether the work scope involves multiple independent items. If file count exceeds batch_size for the stage, spawn parallel instances — do NOT assign all work to a single teammate. Context exhaustion from overloading one teammate costs more than coordination overhead. Default to parallel when in doubt.
